fundamental.headline: Weak business, fair vs itself, expensive vs peers
fundamental.health: Sales down 3% over the last year, it keeps 20 cents of every sales dollar as free cash, its debt is easily covered by earnings.
fundamental.price_text: You're paying about its usual price: its price vs sales is in the middle of its 5-year range. However, it looks cheaper than similar companies once growth is considered. But similar companies as a group are priced near the top of their own 5-year range (their typical price vs sales is higher than 82% of the last 5 years), so "fair" here means fair for an expensive group.
drivers: Profit margins are shrinking: it keeps less of each sale than a year ago.
It is buying back shares, which grows each shareholder's slice.
news: Recent earnings/results news is news with no clear direction for the company; the stock already reacted, so much of it is likely in the price, and it could matter for months.

fundamental.take: The business is struggling to grow profits; there are better places to put money right now. Note: similar companies are all priced near their 5-year highs, so this fair price leaves less room for error than usual. This is research, not personal advice.

deeper.title: What the price assumes
deeper.text: The price assumes about 8% a year growth in free cash flow for 10 years, then 3% (discount rate 9.8% = 10-year Treasury 4.8% + 5%; base: last 12 months of free cash flow). For comparison, sales grew -3% last year; 6%/yr over 3 years — roughly in line with its recent growth.

deeper.title: Signed future revenue
deeper.text: Customer prepayments not yet earned (deferred revenue): $200M, down 53% from a year ago.

deeper.title: Earnings-quality red flags
flags: Inventory up 32% vs quarterly sales up -8% (days of inventory 118 → 155). Products may be building up unsold — a warning sign in chip cycles.
Profit leans on non-operating gains: net income $13.6B vs operating income $8.7B over the last 12 months (e.g. investment gains or one-offs that may not repeat).

deeper.title: Multi-year view
deeper.text: Sales grew 6%/yr over 3 years and 5%/yr over 5 years; operating margin today 20% vs a 5-year range of 20–36% (median 27%): near the bottom of its range (possible cycle low).
deeper.margin_position: near the bottom of its range (possible cycle low)

deeper.title: Cash returned to shareholders
deeper.text: Returned $7.8B to shareholders over the last 12 months ($7.8B buybacks + $0M dividends) = 4.4% of the company's market value. Share count down 2.7% from a year ago (buybacks outpacing stock pay).

deeper.title: Analyst estimates
deeper.text: Next year's earnings-per-share estimate $12.25, down 6% in 90 days (down 5% in the last 30); 0 analysts raised, 4 cut in 30 days. This year's earnings-per-share estimate $9.60, down 6% in 90 days (down 5% in the last 30); 1 analyst raised, 4 cut in 30 days. Source: Yahoo (unofficial).

tiles.title: Earnings per share
tiles.sub: -28% vs a year ago · $12.75 over 12 months (GAAP)
tiles.read: Both profit per share and sales are flat or down from a year ago: no growth right now.
tiles.explain: EPS = profit divided by the number of shares. The quarterly figures are the 'adjusted' EPS analysts track (Yahoo); the 12-month figure is the official GAAP number from SEC filings.

tiles.title: Earnings vs forecasts
tiles.sub: last 8 reports · bars = EPS beat (+) or miss (−) vs the average forecast
tiles.read: A mixed record: 7 beats in the last 8 quarters, so results are hard to predict.
tiles.explain: A 'beat' means reported EPS came in above the average analyst forecast. Source: Yahoo (unofficial).

tiles.title: Sales growth
tiles.read: Sales fell 8% from a year ago: the business is shrinking right now.
tiles.explain: Growth of quarterly sales (revenue) compared with the same quarter a year earlier.

tiles.title: Profit margins
tiles.read: Each $100 of sales leaves $20 of operating profit, down from $28 a year ago: profitability is slipping.
tiles.explain: Operating margin = operating profit ÷ sales. Gross margin = what's left after the direct cost of the product.

tiles.title: Free cash flow
tiles.read: Only 63% of reported profit became spare cash, usually because of heavy investment; worth watching.
tiles.explain: Free cash flow = cash from operations minus spending on equipment and buildings: money the company could return or reinvest.

tiles.title: Price vs profits (P/E)
tiles.read: You pay 13× last year's profit (lower than 77% of the last 5 years).
tiles.explain: P/E = share price ÷ earnings per share. Forward P/E uses next year's forecast earnings.

tiles.title: Next earnings
tiles.read: Reports Feb 3; analysts expect EPS of $2.25, down 36% from a year ago. It usually moves about 7% the day after, so expect a swing.
tiles.explain: Consensus = the average analyst forecast (Yahoo, unofficial). The typical move is the average size of the stock's next-day move after its last reports, not an options-implied figure.

tiles.title: Company outlook
tiles.read: No numeric outlook was found in the latest earnings release, so the next report carries more surprise risk.
tiles.explain: Guidance = what management says it expects for the next quarter or year, from its 8-K earnings release.

tiles.title: Forecast changes
tiles.read: Next year's EPS forecast is down 6% in 90 days (0 raised, 4 cut lately): forecasts are falling.
tiles.explain: How the average analyst forecast for next year's earnings per share changed (Yahoo, unofficial).
